% xr's old release, which \usepackage{xr}[=v5] loads, with its
% \externaldocument in the preamble before xr-hyper and hyperref, which
% load later. The labels of that file are read at the beginning of the
% document, after xr-hyper has replaced the old release's commands. The
% page builds, and each reference prints as with the old release alone:
% from an .aux that LaTeX wrote under hyperref, its number, page, name, and
% \autoref as in the PDF, with no link. A later \externaldocument is
% xr-hyper's: from an .aux that tex4ht wrote under hyperref, with its
% .xref, a link to that document's page.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{xr}[=v5]
\externaldocument[X-]{test-xr/latex}
\usepackage{xr-hyper}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\externaldocument[H-]{test-xr/hyper4ht-hyper}
\begin{document}
CaseM \ref{X-ss}, page \pageref{X-front}, named \nameref{X-thm},
auto \autoref{X-thm}.

CaseN \ref{H-oss}.

Included \ref{X-c}.

\section{Here}\label{here}
Local \ref{here}.
\end{document}
